summary.intent: Use the GSD manager dashboard to drive the final phases (76, 78, 79) of the v2.0 CipherBox milestone to completion — plan, execute, verify, and ship them via parallel background agents — then triage the accumulated todo backlog into closeout phases before marking the milestone done.
summary.outcome: Phases 76 and 79 were fully shipped and merged (PR #610, #611); a todo-triage pass retired 6 resolved todos and defined 4 new closeout phases (80-83), merged via PR #612; Phase 78 (recovery tool) was executed, UAT-resolved, and shipped as PR #613 (conflict-resolved, CI running, unmerged); a ship-workflow fix (draft-PR-first ordering) was opened as PR #614. Milestone was still open at session end, pending PR #613 merge and phases 80-83.

repo: GSD phase branches follow `feat/{slug}` convention; the GSD commit helper auto-switches a worktree onto `phase_branch_template: feat/{slug}` on first commit rather than committing to the ephemeral `worktree-agent-*` branch — but this is inconsistent (happened for phase 79's planner, not phase 76's), so always verify which branch actually received commits before merge-back.
`EnterWorktree` refuses a repo-root→worktree switch on this host; background agents must instead drive worktrees via absolute paths / `git -C` rather than relying on cwd switching.

cipher-box CI's `pr-release-preview` workflow triggers on PR `opened` (including drafts, no draft guard), while `.coderabbit.yaml` has `drafts: false` so CodeRabbit skips draft PRs — meaning `/ship-phase` should open PRs as draft first (let the release bot post `chore(release)`), then mark ready so CodeRabbit reviews the final head, avoiding a race between the release-bot commit and CodeRabbit's review.

Recovery tool v3 must be infra-independent: reuse only `packages/crypto` + `packages/core` (no SDK, no CipherBox API, no Web3Auth), performing a standalone IPNS→IPFS walk via a configurable HTTP gateway, keyed solely off the user-supplied privateKey.

There are two unrelated things both loosely called 'D-07' in this repo: the Rust/FUSE write-plane(UUID)/read-plane(ipnsName) invariant (already enforced) vs. the actual in-scope web/SDK import boundary (`apps/web/src` must not import runtime bindings from sdk-core/core or call raw IPFS) — always disambiguate via the source todo before writing CONTEXT.md decisions.
`ipns@10.1.3`'s `IPNSRecord.validity` is an RFC3339 string, not a `Date` — code assuming `Date` must map via `new Date(record.validity)`.

Folder identity in the read-plane is intentionally `ipnsName`-keyed, not `Node.id`-keyed; re-keying to UUID reintroduces a known orphaned-store bug — this recurs as a temptation across phases (76, 78, 79) and must be explicitly rejected each time with rationale recorded so executors don't 'fix' it back.
workflow: When two background executors touching related code (e.g. phases 76 and 79 both touching `useFileBrowserActions.ts`) run in parallel and later need merging, code conflicts often auto-merge cleanly while `.planning/ROADMAP.md`/`STATE.md` bookkeeping files are the actual conflict source — resolve those by keeping both sides' completion markers rather than picking one.

For long-running parallel background pipelines with a shared exclusive resource (e.g. the SDK E2E gate binding :3000 and resetting Postgres/Kubo), that gate must be serialized across concurrent ship runs even if the rest of the pipeline can run in parallel.

After a session hits its quota limit mid-execution, background agents that commit atomically per plan preserve resumable progress; resuming in the *same* worktree (not a fresh one) preserves partial commits and installed `node_modules`, which is faster and safer than restarting from scratch.

A killed/stopped background agent (via TaskStop or user interrupt) cannot be resumed via SendMessage — the orchestrator must either dispatch a fresh agent or, for small mechanical steps (like resolving a merge conflict), do the work inline itself.

Session-scoped cron jobs (via CronCreate) are best-effort: they survive quota throttling (session alive but rate-limited) but do not survive a full session exit, and firing the cron only delivers a prompt for the orchestrator to act on — it does not autonomously resume interrupted work by itself.

friction: Two background executors (Phase 76 and 79) were both killed mid-run by hitting the session's Anthropic quota limit simultaneously, losing significant unpushed background progress until manually resumed.

The Phase 76 ship agent initially misreported CI as fully green while `Cargo Check & Test (Windows)` was actually failing (root cause: a test-only invalid-UUID string in the ported D-07 regression test), requiring the agent to self-correct.

A `git rebase` of 40 commits from `feat/79` onto updated `main` was abandoned mid-way due to a recurring `.planning/STATE.md` bookkeeping conflict on every replayed commit; switched to a single `git merge` instead, which resolved the conflict once.

The 'Ship Phase 78' background agent was accidentally stopped by the user mid-pipeline (after opening PR #613 but before finishing conflict resolution/review triage), and could not be resumed via SendMessage, forcing the orchestrator to finish the remaining steps (conflict resolution, learnings doc, CI monitoring) inline instead of via a background agent.
A `git push` to `feat/78` hit a transient DNS failure requiring a retry.

The GSD commit helper reported a false-negative `commit_failed` status for the Phase 78 discuss-artifacts commit even though the commit had actually landed cleanly (a previously known/memory-flagged issue).
open_items: PR #613 (Phase 78 recovery-tool ship) is open, CI running, not yet merged — user's call to merge.
PR #614 (ship-workflow draft-PR-first fix) is open, not yet merged.

Phase 76's `76-05` Windows D-07 code needed a pre-merge CI gate that was eventually cleared, but 2 out-of-scope P1 follow-up todos were logged from Greptile review: vault-init register-retry dead-end, and TEE renewal over-rejecting longer-lived records.

Four new closeout phases (80: Rotation Write-Plane & Re-Mint Durability [HIGH], 81: TEE Republish & IPNS-Record Correctness, 82: Wire-Encoding Domain Hardening [HIGH], 83: Desktop Resilience) are defined in ROADMAP but not yet discussed/planned — explicitly held until Phase 78 fully lands.

A v2.1 backlog was identified but left in `pending/todos`: web polish/observability/a11y cluster, ops/CI hygiene chores, Tier-3 large-file refactor, plus three defer-forever v2.1+ features (ERC-1271 contract-wallet auth, CRDT IPNS inbox sharing, alternative MFA factor types).

Phase 78's formal verification flagged 2 UAT items (poll-monotonicity clean-DB re-run, SC2 spinner-visibility assertion) as `human_needed`; these were addressed during the ship pipeline but should be double-checked given the interrupted/resumed agent history.

The `extract-learnings` step of `/ship-phase` for Phase 78 was not reached by the (stopped) ship agent; the orchestrator authored `78-LEARNINGS.md` manually inline instead — worth confirming it matches what the automated step would have produced.
